id: title:Piccirello:scope bearer token introspection to the caller

review.posthog_relevance: Adds bearer-token ownership checks and clarifies OAuth introspection behavior, establishing application identity before token lookup to prevent privilege escalation and unauthorized cross-client token access.
review.reason: The change implements bearer-token ownership checks and documentation clarifying OAuth introspection behavior. P1.F3.H3 and P1.F3.H2 establish the caller's access token identity, while P1.F1.H1 documents the scope restriction. This represents a substantive, bounded correctness and security improvement.
review.uncertainty: The exact runtime behavior and complete implementation details are not fully visible; the tier relies on the presence of ownership checks and documentation rather than demonstrated execution or comprehensive test results.

observations.limitations: This chunk is a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No missing context. No abstention.

observations.behavior: Documentation and test changes. Documentation: P1.F1.H1. Tests: P1.F2.H1.
observations.code_quote: This means you can introspect any token using your application's client credentials, regardless of what scopes the token being introspected has. However, if you want to use an access token to introspect other tokens, that access token must have been granted the `introspection` scope.
observations.posthog_connection: Clarifies OAuth introspection behavior: bearer tokens with introspection scope can only read tokens from the same application, not arbitrary tokens. This prevents privilege escalation where a bearer token could read other clients' tokens.

observations.behavior: Adds bearer-token ownership check. P1.F3.H3, P1.F3.H4, P1.F3.H5.
observations.posthog_connection: Records the caller's access token to establish application identity before token lookup. This establishes the basis for the ownership check.
